# NEXUS — ML Research Platform

> A no-code research platform fusing **mathematical optimization** with
> machine learning. Built by Dr. Kobkoon Janngam at the Department of
> Mathematics, Chiang Mai University. Used as a showcase for fixed-point
> ELM (Extreme Learning Machine) reformulated as a convex minimization
> problem, with end-to-end data cleaning and pretrained AI inference.

The platform is split into three modules. Each module is a fully working
research demo intended for academic exploration — not a commercial product.

## Quick facts

- **Author**: Dr. Kobkoon Janngam, Chiang Mai University
- **Domain**: https://ml-research-platform.vercel.app/
- **Type**: Web application (research showcase)
- **Stack**: React 19 + Vite + Tailwind frontend, FastAPI + scikit-learn + PyTorch backend
- **License**: Research/academic use; bundled YOLOv8 is AGPL-3.0
- **Target audience**: ML researchers, optimization theorists, graduate students

## Modules

### Module 1 — Data Forensic & Cleaning
- URL: https://ml-research-platform.vercel.app/forensic
- Purpose: Automated EDA + preprocessing pipeline (missing values, outliers,
  scaling, encoding, feature selection, imbalance handling, drop columns)
- Key features: Per-fold leakage-safe transforms, K-Fold/Stratified/Holdout
  cross-validation, Pearson/Spearman/Kendall correlation, distribution stats
  (skewness/kurtosis), Cramér's V categorical association, before/after
  preview, undo, export to CSV/Excel/Python script

### Module 2 — ELM Studio
- URL: https://ml-research-platform.vercel.app/elm-studio
- Purpose: Train Extreme Learning Machine models via closed-form
  least-squares (Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse), with future support for
  fixed-point + convex-reformulation training (Janngam et al., in progress)
- Key features: Adaptive hidden-node defaults (10×features), 3 activation
  functions (sigmoid/relu/tanh), live cross-validation metrics, learning
  curve, calibration diagram, model export as .joblib bundle

### Module 3 — AI Model Hub
- URL: https://ml-research-platform.vercel.app/deep-learning
- Purpose: Curated pretrained AI models for vision tasks
- Image Classification: ImageNet (EfficientNetV2-S, 83.9% top-1), Food-101, Birds-525
- Medical Imaging: Chest X-ray (torchxrayvision DenseNet121, 18 pathologies)
  with Grad-CAM attention; Skin-lesion ViT classifier; Brain-tumor MRI ViT
- Object Detection: YOLOv8n animal detection, 17-keypoint pose estimation,
  80-class general COCO objects (AGPL-3.0)
- Tabular: Coming soon (Titanic survival, heart disease, wine quality)

## Key research themes

- Mathematical optimization for machine learning
- Fixed-point algorithms and Banach contraction principle
- Extreme Learning Machine convex reformulation
- Pipeline-bound preprocessing (zero data leakage in cross-validation)
- Pretrained model inference with attention visualization (Grad-CAM)

## Acknowledgements

- ImageNet (Russakovsky et al., 2015) — EfficientNetV2-S backbone
- COCO 2017 (Lin et al., 2014) — YOLOv8 detection
- torchxrayvision (Cohen et al., 2022) — chest X-ray classifier
- ISIC 2019 — skin-lesion benchmark
- scikit-learn (Pedregosa et al., 2011) — preprocessing + base classifiers
- PyTorch + torchvision (Paszke et al., 2019)

## Disclaimer

All medical-imaging models are research-only pattern-matching tools.
They are NOT FDA-cleared and must NOT be used for clinical diagnosis.
Only qualified specialists can diagnose medical images.
